Hair loss may still be associated with getting older, but two large datasets of Indian men seeking help for hair loss suggest that the concern is appearing much earlier than many might assume. An analysis of more than 12.6 lakh hair-loss consultations and assessments from Man Matters and Traya Health shows a consistent pattern: men are seeking help for hair loss predominantly in their 20s and early 30s, while a significant number are already experiencing noticeable progression when they do. The datasets are separate and cover different consultation populations and periods. The Man Matters Hairfall Index 2026 analysed 704,152 consultations conducted between August 2025 and August 2026, while a Traya Health study looked at 561,960 Indian men seeking help for hair loss. Together, the numbers offer a snapshot of when men start seeking help, what they notice first and how hair loss appears to progress with age. The Man Matters data found that 87.2% of hairfall consultations came from men under 35, with men in their 20s accounting for a significant share of the consultation base. Traya’s study similarly found that the median age of men experiencing hair loss was 29, with 76.4% of those assessed below 35.
